subject: Clarifying hosting modes for SIG: hosted vs dedicated vs private (concise evidence plan)
messages:

Subject: SIG follow-up: hosting modes and evidence required

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks for taking this on. Our SIG review team needs clear, short-form answers that explain how Redwood's three hosting modes differ for security/control purposes, and which artifacts you can provide for each (e.g., network diagrams, SOC 2 scoping notes, encryption key custody statements, evidence of tenant isolation).

Primary asks:
- A concise paragraph for each mode (Hosted, Dedicated, Private/VPC/on-prem) focused on data residency, customer control over keys, network access, and audit log availability.
- A list of specific artifacts you can attach for each mode and approximate delivery timelines.

We need something we can drop into our SIG spreadsheet and share with our GRC team. Can you also indicate if any items require an NDA or on-site review?

Appreciate it — ideally something by EOD Friday so we can keep our procurement schedule.

Best,
Jonas

FinServCorp

From: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com

Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: hosting modes and evidence required

Jonas —

Thanks, jumping on this. I put together the short explainer below (formatted so you can paste into SIG cells), plus an attachments manifest. Rafael (infra) and Laura (compliance) are looped to confirm artifact availability and ETA.

Hosted (Redwood API - multi-tenant):
- Short answer: Fully-managed, multi-tenant hosted service where Redwood controls the runtime and storage. Customer data is logically segregated; no customer-managed keys in the standard plan.
- Security/control notes: Data encrypted in transit and at rest using Redwood-managed keys (AES-256). SOC 2 controls cover the hosted environment. Customers can request VPC egress & private peering for network isolation on certain plans.
- Artifacts available: SOC 2 Type II report (redacted), hosted network flow diagram (logical), data retention policy excerpt, pen-test summary.
- ETA / gating: Most artifacts available under NDA within 2 business days; SOC 2 redaction takes 3 business days. Private peering configuration requires account onboarding (1-2 weeks).

Dedicated (reserved capacity - customer-isolated GPU pools):
- Short answer: Dedicated GPU pools that are logically isolated for a customer within Redwood's environment; stronger tenancy guarantees and configurable autoscaling. Customer data remains on infrastructure allocated to the customer but still managed by Redwood ops unless Private is chosen.
- Security/control notes: Option to use customer-managed KMS (bring-your-own-key) for disk and object storage encryption in Dedicated deployments. Network isolation (dedicated VPC) is configurable; audit logs and per-tenant telemetry are available.
- Artifacts available: Dedicated topology diagram, KMS integration guide (how BYOK works), per-tenant logging sample (anonymized), configuration checklist for Dedicated onboarding.
- ETA / gating: Topology diagram and checklist: 1 business day. BYOK guide and log samples: 3 business days. Some items require an account-level contract amendment.

Private / VPC / On‑prem (customer-managed):
- Short answer: Control plane (optionally hosted) with runtime deployed inside customer VPC or on-prem hardware. Customer has the highest degree of control, including full network control, access policies, and local key management.
- Security/control notes: Can be deployed air-gapped or with controlled egress. Customer controls KMS/HSM; Redwood provides deployment automation and a minimal operator bundle. Audit evidence is collected locally; Redwood can ship configuration checklists for compliance teams.
- Artifacts available: Deployment architecture diagram (customer-specific), operator runbook, KMS/HSM integration checklist, SLA/managed-support scope.
- ETA / gating: Diagrams and checklists: typically 2-3 business days but often require a short discovery call. On‑site reviews or air‑gapped evidence collection require separate SOW and timeline (2-4 weeks).

Attachments manifest (what I can attach now):
- redwood_deployment_modes_SIG_excerpt.pdf — concise summary of the three modes and references to controls (2 pages).
- network_diagram_vpc.png — sample Dedicated/VPC topology (anonymized).
- SIG_response_manifest.csv — quick mapping from SIG questions to artifact names/locations.

NDA / on-site notes: SOC 2 full report and some redacted security artifacts require an executed NDA. On-site or air-gapped evidence collection requires SOW and scheduling.

Next steps: Rafael and Laura, can you confirm the attachments and whether we should redact any items before sending? Jonas — if helpful, we can do a 30-min call to walk your GRC person through the artifacts.

Thanks,

Stephanie Nguyen
